evals.name: new-external-service
evals.expected_output: Does not jump straight into a raw-smtplib EmailSender class. Surveys real options (managed transactional-email service and/or a library that handles deliverability/retry/TLS), recognizes this is material (new external service or dependency, no existing internal option), and produces a decision brief with an explicit pause for a human choice.
expectations: Does not proceed straight to implementing the raw-smtplib EmailSender class as the delivered solution
Produces something recognizable as a decision brief: options considered, a recommendation, and consequences of owning the chosen option
States plainly that implementation is paused pending a human decision, rather than proceeding

evals.name: existing-internal-reuse
evals.expected_output: Discovers and reuses the existing app/utils/ids.py generate_id() helper, already used the same way twice elsewhere. Not material -- no decision brief, no gate, just reuse.
expectations: The implementation calls (or clearly plans to call) the existing generate_id() helper rather than writing new ID-generation logic
No decision brief, options table, or explicit pause for a human choice is produced
Does not treat this as needing a formal survey of internal/platform/library/service/custom options

evals.name: trivial-local-helper
evals.expected_output: Just gives the one-line strftime formatting call. No build-vs-adopt apparatus of any kind -- local code is obviously simpler and no dependency is seriously in contention.
expectations: Gives a direct, minimal answer (the strftime/format call) with no decision brief, options table, or solution-space survey
Does not raise or consider adopting a dependency for this
Response length/structure stays proportional to the triviality of the ask

evals.name: conventional-dependency-use
evals.expected_output: Applies the existing slowapi @limiter.limit(...) pattern, already used identically on two other routes, to the new endpoint. Already a project convention -- not material, no gate.
expectations: Implements the rate limit using the existing limiter/slowapi pattern, not a new hand-rolled limiter or a newly-introduced different dependency
No decision brief, options table, or explicit pause for a human choice is produced
Treats this as an ordinary use of an already-adopted dependency, not a new decision

evals.name: unrelated-bug-fix
evals.expected_output: Just fixes the off-by-one bug (< becomes <=). Nothing build-vs-adopt-shaped in the response at all -- this task has nothing to do with sourcing a capability.
expectations: The off-by-one bug is fixed correctly
Nothing in the response resembles a build-vs-adopt decision brief, options table, solution-space survey, or materiality discussion
No mention of dependencies, libraries, services, or ownership tradeoffs anywhere in the response

evals.name: already-decided-dont-reask
evals.expected_output: An applicable recorded decision (ADR-0004) already resolves custom vs. Celery+Redis for this exact requirement. Proceeds toward implementing the custom Postgres-backed JobQueue without re-opening the choice -- no decision brief, no options table, no pause.
expectations: No decision brief, options table, or explicit pause for a human choice is produced
The response proceeds toward implementing the custom Postgres-backed JobQueue consistent with ADR-0004
Does not treat the existing ADR as merely a preference that needs to be re-weighed from scratch
